attempted_axis: Reopen-triage drive of the 2026-08-30 park: measured the residual first, proved an exact arithmetic model of the 4-instruction surplus, and REFUTED the park's stated mechanism - the seven loop-invariant literal loads are hoisted into callee-saved FPRs on BOTH sides, so the residual is block PLACEMENT, not hoisting.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.r0-homed-address-temp-forces-the-indexed-store-form.20260901.v1 APPLIED, and its precondition MEASURABLY HOLDS at three sites here - a THIRD confirming function for that law, in the target-longer direction, and it post-dates this park. Aligned view at +0x144: target `add r3,r29,r27` + `li r0,0` + `stb r0,1152(r3)` homes the stored VALUE in r0 and the address temp in a general register; ours `addi r0,r27,1152` + `li r3,0` + `stbx r3,r31,r0` homes the ADDRESS TEMP in r0, which is architecturally illegal as a displacement base and forces the indexed store. Same at +0x180 and +0x208. TWO axes spent trying to reassociate it, both byte-IDENTICAL, which kills the axis under the two-identical-A/Bs rule: (1) member form via a typed view local, `base->caption_line_buf[output_len]`; (2) explicit POINTER-add association, `*((u8*)base + output_len + offsetof(AuxSceneView, caption_line_buf))`. MWCC canonicalises base + i + K to base + (i + K) regardless of how the source associates it, so the store form is not reachable by index or member spelling here either - consistent with the law's own finding on sndFxInitVoices and fn_80051164. claim.law.member-form-does-not-restore-preoffset-association.20260831.v1 APPLIED and independently re-confirmed by axis 1; it should have been screened BEFORE that probe was spent and is the reason axis 2 was not worth its build in hindsight. claim.law.mwcc-ctr-loop-strength-reduction-is-defeated-by-an-in-body-exit-test.20260831.v1 NOT APPLICABLE: neither side emits mtctr/bdnz, the loop is a byte-comparison scan with a switch. claim.law.block-allocation-order-is-textual-not-nesting-depth.20260831.v1 SCREENED as the closest-shaped law for the surviving placement residual and is the right family, but it names no lever that reaches a hoisted-CONSTANT block. claim.law.insn-count-parity-outranks-local-opcode-fidelity.20260831.v1 SCREENED and pointedly NOT decisive here: neither state has parity (baseline +4, while-form -1), so it cannot arbitrate, and fuzzy had to. claim.law.fuzzy-can-underweight-a-real-improvement.20260830.v1 SCREENED and DECLINED: it licenses the finer metric on a SMALL function with a marginal dip, and a 2.24-point drop on a 177-instruction function that also moves project fuzzy is not that case. claim.law.real-can-underweight-a-large-alignment-gain-so-arbitrate-conflicts-on-fuzzy.20260831.v1 APPLIED as the governing arbitration rule. opt_common_subs was flipped on for this function as a one-off probe (the pragma region at auxscreen.c:884-990 contains ONLY CaptionTextSub, so the flip was sibling-safe) on the theory that disabled CSE suppressed the hoist; measured NEUTRAL, restored - the hoist is not CSE-gated. claim.law.webfrank-pinned-function-source-freeze.20260831.v1 SCREENED: game/ui/auxscreen has no pinned functions.
attributes.residual: PARKED at the pre-existing best (real 172, insns T177/O181, multiset 20t, fuzzy 88.2775) after arbitration, but the mechanism is now modelled exactly rather than described. COUNT MODEL, proven: our 4-instruction surplus is +5 minus 1. The +5 is an entry GUARD we emit and target does not - ours `lwz gGameMode; addis; cmplwi; beq ->exit; lfd; fcmpo; ble ->exit` (6 words) against target's single `b ->22c` at +0xdc. The -1 is the site-3 store cluster where target spends an extra `mr r0,r27` (3 words) and we spend 2. Both sides then carry a byte-IDENTICAL 6-word bottom test (`lwz gGameMode; addis; cmplwi; beq; fcmpo; bgt ->body`). So target compiled a plain pre-tested `while`, entered by jumping to the bottom test, while our source spells the AGENTS-era `if (cond) { do { ... } while (cond); }`. CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: converting to `while` moved real 172 -> 159, insns 181 -> 176, multiset 20t -> 13t, and reproduced the prior session's axis-1 numbers to four decimals. THE PARK'S FRAMING IS REFUTED. It states the target 'hoists seven loop-invariant literal/conversion loads before its entry branch', implying we fail to hoist them. We do hoist them: both objects load all seven ONCE into callee-saved f26-f31 plus a `lis` (both save f22-f31), so the loop-invariant motion is identical. The only difference is which BLOCK the hoisted group is laid out in - target places it in the preheader ahead of the body, we place it adjacent to the bottom test - and the two layouts contain the SAME 16 instructions in that region (target 10 top + 6 bottom, ours 3 top + 13 bottom). That is a layout permutation, not a missing optimisation, and it is why objdiff punishes the `while` form so hard: seven previously position-matched instructions relocate. ARBITRATION, and the reason nothing structural was retained: fuzzy 88.2775 -> 86.0396 and project Game Code fuzzy 97.69 -> 97.68 against real 172 -> 159. Three structural indicators improve and the two scoring metrics regress; AGENTS.md's 'preserve the best verified project-level result' governs and the prior session's revert is CONFIRMED CORRECT on an independent re-measurement. UNPARK CONDITION, now specific: the `while` form is the CORRECT PLATFORM and is blocked by exactly two things - (a) the 7-word hoisted-constant block placement, and (b) the 3-site indexed-store class below. Close (a) and the function reaches 177/177 with a multiset near 6t and a fuzzy far above the current baseline; until (a) has a lever, do not retain the `while` form.
